title: The AI Shelf: Sustainable Apparel
description: How Canadian apparel brands appeared across shopping prompts in ChatGPT and Google AI Mode.

sections.heading: Different systems, different shelves
sections.body: Only three of eight unbranded prompts shared any brand between the two systems. In this sample, a single prompt or platform would have given an incomplete view of brand visibility.

sections.heading: Brand presence and source presence are separate
sections.body: tentree appeared in eight of the sixteen unbranded answers. The report also recorded different linking patterns: Google AI Mode returned more distinct source links, while ChatGPT linked more heavily to brand websites.

sections.heading: What I would investigate next
sections.body: Repeat the prompts over time, separate recommendations from incidental mentions, and compare product attributes with the sources attached to each answer. These observations suggest questions for testing; they do not establish ranking factors.

methodology: Twelve prompts across awareness, consideration and decision stages, run in two systems on 22 October 2026 in Vancouver. ChatGPT used temporary chats; Google AI Mode was signed in. Brand mentions and visible links were recorded.
limitations: A small, one-day snapshot. Location, account context and answer variability can affect results. Brand matching can include linked brands. No traffic, sales or causal effects were measured.
